children: Fast food chain Steak n Shake has formally endorsed two Ohio Republicans as it continues to lean into the "Make America Healthy Again" campaign.
The political endorsements extend a broader brand repositioning as Steak n Shake has embraced beef-tallow fries, butter-based buns, cane-sugar Coca-Cola
products, a “Chief MAHA Officer,” large American flags, Tesla
Superchargers, and social media posts highlighting visits at its restaurants by Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and other Republican figures who visit its restaurants.

A publicly traded restaurant company openly endorsing candidates is highly unusual, as usually corporations influence politics through donations, PACs, and trade groups rather than official campaign endorsements.

Steak n Shake’s recent operating history may help explain the strategy reset. After the chain posted losses in 2018 and 2019 and then abandoned its longtime full-service format, it invested roughly $50M in remodels, kiosks, and a counter-/self-service model while reducing hours and simplifying the menu. The turnaround has been profitable, but Steak n Shake has closed or refranchised hundreds of restaurants from its 2018 peak store count level.
The Steak n Shake chain is owned by Bigali Holdings

title: Steak n Shake endorses political candidates in unusual move for a public restaurant company
